func TestDeleteUser(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("normal", func(t *testing.T) {
		db.LoadAndAssertFixtures(t)
		s := db.NewSession()
		defer s.Close()
		notifications.Fake()
		t.Cleanup(notifications.Unfake)

		u := &user.User{ID: 6}
		err := DeleteUser(s, u)

		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.NoError(t, s.Commit())
		db.AssertMissing(t, "users", map[string]interface{}{"id": u.ID})
		db.AssertMissing(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 24}) // only user6 had access to this project
		db.AssertExists(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 6}, false)
		db.AssertExists(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 7}, false)
		db.AssertExists(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 8}, false)
		db.AssertExists(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 9}, false)
		db.AssertExists(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 10}, false)
		db.AssertExists(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 11}, false)
	})
	t.Run("user with no projects", func(t *testing.T) {
		db.LoadAndAssertFixtures(t)
		s := db.NewSession()
		defer s.Close()
		notifications.Fake()
		t.Cleanup(notifications.Unfake)

		u := &user.User{ID: 4}
		err := DeleteUser(s, u)

		require.NoError(t, err)
		// No assertions for deleted projects since that user doesn't have any
	})
	t.Run("user with a default project", func(t *testing.T) {
		db.LoadAndAssertFixtures(t)
		s := db.NewSession()
		defer s.Close()
		notifications.Fake()
		t.Cleanup(notifications.Unfake)

		u := &user.User{ID: 16}
		err := DeleteUser(s, u)

		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.NoError(t, s.Commit())
		db.AssertMissing(t, "users", map[string]interface{}{"id": u.ID})
		db.AssertMissing(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 37}) // only user16 had access to this project, and it was their default
	})
	t.Run("disabled user", func(t *testing.T) {
		db.LoadAndAssertFixtures(t)
		s := db.NewSession()
		defer s.Close()
		notifications.Fake()
		t.Cleanup(notifications.Unfake)

		u := &user.User{ID: 17}
		err := DeleteUser(s, u)

		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.NoError(t, s.Commit())
		db.AssertMissing(t, "users", map[string]interface{}{"id": u.ID})
	})
	t.Run("disabled user with task attachment they created", func(t *testing.T) {
		// Regression test: the cascade calls TaskAttachment.Delete -> ReadOne,
		// which loads the attachment's creator via user.GetUserByID. If the
		// creator is the disabled user being deleted, that lookup must not
		// surface ErrAccountDisabled out of the cascade.
		db.LoadAndAssertFixtures(t)
		s := db.NewSession()
		defer s.Close()
		notifications.Fake()
		t.Cleanup(notifications.Unfake)

		project := &Project{
			Title:   "disabled user project",
			OwnerID: 17,
		}
		insertTestProject(t, s, project)

		task := &Task{
			Title:       "disabled user task",
			ProjectID:   project.ID,
			CreatedByID: 17,
			Index:       1,
		}
		_, err := s.Insert(task)
		require.NoError(t, err)

		_, err = s.Insert(&TaskAttachment{
			TaskID:      task.ID,
			FileID:      1,
			CreatedByID: 17,
		})
		require.NoError(t, err)

		err = DeleteUser(s, &user.User{ID: 17})
		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.NoError(t, s.Commit())
		db.AssertMissing(t, "users", map[string]interface{}{"id": 17})
		db.AssertMissing(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": project.ID})
		db.AssertMissing(t, "tasks", map[string]interface{}{"id": task.ID})
	})

func TestDeleteUser(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("normal", func(t *testing.T) {
		db.LoadAndAssertFixtures(t)
		s := db.NewSession()
		defer s.Close()
		notifications.Fake()
		t.Cleanup(notifications.Unfake)

		u := &user.User{ID: 6}
		err := DeleteUser(s, u)

		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.NoError(t, s.Commit())
		db.AssertMissing(t, "users", map[string]interface{}{"id": u.ID})
		db.AssertMissing(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 24}) // only user6 had access to this project
		db.AssertExists(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 6}, false)
		db.AssertExists(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 7}, false)
		db.AssertExists(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 8}, false)
		db.AssertExists(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 9}, false)
		db.AssertExists(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 10}, false)
		db.AssertExists(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 11}, false)
	})
	t.Run("user with no projects", func(t *testing.T) {
		db.LoadAndAssertFixtures(t)
		s := db.NewSession()
		defer s.Close()
		notifications.Fake()
		t.Cleanup(notifications.Unfake)

		u := &user.User{ID: 4}
		err := DeleteUser(s, u)

		require.NoError(t, err)
		// No assertions for deleted projects since that user doesn't have any
	})
	t.Run("user with a default project", func(t *testing.T) {
		db.LoadAndAssertFixtures(t)
		s := db.NewSession()
		defer s.Close()
		notifications.Fake()
		t.Cleanup(notifications.Unfake)

		u := &user.User{ID: 16}
		err := DeleteUser(s, u)

		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.NoError(t, s.Commit())
		db.AssertMissing(t, "users", map[string]interface{}{"id": u.ID})
		db.AssertMissing(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": 37}) // only user16 had access to this project, and it was their default
	})
	t.Run("disabled user", func(t *testing.T) {
		db.LoadAndAssertFixtures(t)
		s := db.NewSession()
		defer s.Close()
		notifications.Fake()
		t.Cleanup(notifications.Unfake)

		u := &user.User{ID: 17}
		err := DeleteUser(s, u)

		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.NoError(t, s.Commit())
		db.AssertMissing(t, "users", map[string]interface{}{"id": u.ID})
	})
	t.Run("disabled user with task attachment they created", func(t *testing.T) {
		// Regression test: the cascade calls TaskAttachment.Delete -> ReadOne,
		// which loads the attachment's creator via user.GetUserByID. If the
		// creator is the disabled user being deleted, that lookup must not
		// surface ErrAccountDisabled out of the cascade.
		db.LoadAndAssertFixtures(t)
		s := db.NewSession()
		defer s.Close()
		notifications.Fake()
		t.Cleanup(notifications.Unfake)

		project := &Project{
			Title:   "disabled user project",
			OwnerID: 17,
		}
		insertTestProject(t, s, project)

		task := &Task{
			Title:       "disabled user task",
			ProjectID:   project.ID,
			CreatedByID: 17,
			Index:       1,
		}
		_, err := s.Insert(task)
		require.NoError(t, err)

		_, err = s.Insert(&TaskAttachment{
			TaskID:      task.ID,
			FileID:      1,
			CreatedByID: 17,
		})
		require.NoError(t, err)

		err = DeleteUser(s, &user.User{ID: 17})
		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.NoError(t, s.Commit())
		db.AssertMissing(t, "users", map[string]interface{}{"id": 17})
		db.AssertMissing(t, "projects", map[string]interface{}{"id": project.ID})
		db.AssertMissing(t, "tasks", map[string]interface{}{"id": task.ID})
	})
	t.Run("cleans up task assignments and subscriptions", func(t *testing.T) {
		db.LoadAndAssertFixtures(t)
		s := db.NewSession()
		defer s.Close()
		notifications.Fake()
		t.Cleanup(notifications.Unfake)

		task := &Task{
			Title:       "user cleanup",
			ProjectID:   19,
			CreatedByID: 7,
			Index:       4,
		}
		_, err := s.Insert(task)
		require.NoError(t, err)

		_, err = s.Insert(&TaskAssginee{TaskID: task.ID, UserID: 4})
		require.NoError(t, err)

		_, err = s.Insert(&Subscription{EntityType: SubscriptionEntityTask, EntityID: task.ID, UserID: 4})
		require.NoError(t, err)

		_, err = s.Insert(&Subscription{EntityType: SubscriptionEntityProject, EntityID: 19, UserID: 4})
		require.NoError(t, err)

		_, err = s.Insert(&TeamMember{TeamID: 9, UserID: 4})
		require.NoError(t, err)

		err = DeleteUser(s, &user.User{ID: 4})
		require.NoError(t, err)

content.text:
Deleting an account damages other people's data: I ran the real flow across 22 scenarios, and in several of them owners lost their own projects or bystanders gained admin rights. Nothing is fixed, and the throwaway test is removed (tree clean).

## What happened to other people's data

| Situation before the account is deleted | Result after |
|---|---|
| Owner shared a project read-only with the leaver (only share) | Project's owner becomes the deleted user's id. The real owner has no read, write or admin access and it vanishes from their list. Nobody can reach it. |
| Same, but another read-only collaborator was added first | That collaborator becomes owner and admin. The real owner is locked out. |
| Owner's Inbox shared read-only with the leaver | Same loss, on their default project. |
| Owner shared a parent project read-only | Parent is lost to the owner; the child stays reachable. |
| Owner shared write with a bystander, read with the leaver | Bystander is promoted from write to admin. Owner keeps access. |
| Project shared with a team (read or write), leaver is a member | The team's share becomes admin, so every remaining member becomes project admin. |
| Leaver's team has no other members | The empty team stays and now holds admin on the other person's project. |
| Leaver owns an unshared parent; someone else owns a sub-project under it | The other person's sub-project, its tasks and its attachment file are deleted. |

## The leaver's own things

- **Own project, read-only collaborator:** the collaborator becomes owner and admin, which looks like the intended handover.
- **Own project, write/admin collaborator or team:** the project survives and stays usable, but its owner points at a user that no longer exists.
- **Own unshared projects:** deleted cleanly, including attachment files.
- **Teams:** memberships are removed. A team where the leaver was the only admin is left with no admin; the remaining member cannot update it, delete it or add members.
- **Avatar and data-export zip:** both stay in the database and in storage. The export cleanup cron finds files through the user row (`pkg/models/export.go:474`), so it will never remove this one.

## What held up

- Tasks, comments, attachments and labels the leaver created in surviving projects still load without errors; the author just comes back empty.
- Task assignments are removed.
- A link share the leaver created on someone else's project keeps working; the owner can still see and remove it.
- Leftover rows: the leaver's share rows (some promoted to admin) and one saved-filter view with three buckets.

## Cause

`getProjectsToDelete` (`pkg/models/user_delete.go:94`) walks every project the leaver can see, not only the ones they own. For each it runs `ensureProjectAdminUser` (line 205, owner rewrite at 244) and `ensureProjectAdminTeam` (line 252), which promote a share or reassign the owner whenever no share is admin. They also count the leaver's own share row. Separately, `Project.Delete` removes child projects regardless of who owns them (`pkg/models/project.go:1559`).

## How it was run

- **Flow:** `RequestDeletion` → `ConfirmDeletion` → the hourly cron body → `DeleteUser`, with users, projects, shares, teams and uploads created through the normal model methods.
- **Shortcuts:** I planted a confirm token with a known value, because the real one only exists in the email, and I backdated the three-day wait.
- **Sub-project case:** built through the permission-checked path (share, create child, unshare).
- **Not covered:** this ran on the in-memory SQLite test database, not Postgres or MySQL, and not through HTTP. Admin "delete now" and the CLI call the same `DeleteUser`, but I did not run those.

Full output is in `/tmp/claude-0/-exp-PREWORK-0c8u31w5-model-a/53e15d53-b32b-4f2b-bd51-f322f3934f44/scratchpad/del1.log` and `/tmp/claude-0/-exp-PREWORK-0c8u31w5-model-a/53e15d53-b32b-4f2b-bd51-f322f3934f44/scratchpad/del2.log`.

lastPrompt: Good, that's the kind of thing I meant. Same treatment for the sensitive actions now: changing password or email, turning 2fa on and off, export, requesting deletion. For each one, what exactly does i…

content.text:
A stolen session can guess the account password without limit on every one of these actions, and can do real damage without the password at all. I ran each action through the real router on v1 and v2 with a session from the real login endpoint. Nothing is fixed, and the throwaway test is removed (tree clean).

## What each action demands

| Action | Beyond a valid session | Password checked against | Wrong guesses (default config) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Change password | Old password | Account matching the session's username as username *or* email | Unlimited; warning email every 3rd |
| Change email | Password | Same lookup, and the change is applied to the matched account | Unlimited; warning email every 3rd |
| 2FA enroll | Nothing; returns the secret | n/a | n/a |
| 2FA enable | A code from that secret, no password | n/a | n/a |
| 2FA disable | Password, no 2FA code | Caller's own row, by id | Unlimited, silent |
| Export request / download | Password | Caller's own row | Unlimited, silent |
| Deletion request / cancel | Password | Caller's own row | Unlimited, silent |
| Deletion confirm | Emailed token, no password | n/a | n/a |

- None of them asks for a 2FA code.
- Accounts from OIDC or LDAP skip the password for export and deletion: session alone requested an export, downloaded the zip (v2), and requested and cancelled deletion.
- Minting a CalDAV token or API token needs only the session.

## Whose password

- **Normal case:** it is the caller's own. A session for one user plus another user's password got 403 on all 14 endpoints.
- **Exception:** password change and email change look the account up by `username = ? OR email = ?` using the session's username (`pkg/user/user.go:387`).
  - I created an externally provisioned account whose username was `user1@example.com`; `CreateUser` accepted it, though the signup validator rejects that shape for local users.
  - From that account's session, a wrong guess counted against user1.
  - user1's password then changed **user1's** email to the attacker's address (`pkg/user/update_email.go:57` acts on the matched account, not the caller).
- **How that was built:** I called `CreateUser` and `IssueUserToken` directly, the same calls the OIDC flow makes, not through a real identity provider. Which row wins when two match is up to the database; SQLite picked user1.

## What stops guessing

- **Default config:** nothing. On all 14 endpoints, 40 wrong guesses got 40 plain 403s, the account stayed active, and the right password then worked.
- **Password and email change:** each failure is counted and a warning email goes out on every third (13 for 40 guesses). There is no lockout.
- **2FA disable, export, deletion request and cancel:** nothing is counted and no email is sent, so these are a silent password oracle.
- **With `ratelimit.enabled: true`:** on the four endpoints I tried, the 101st request in a minute got 429. That is still 100 guesses a minute, and it blocks the real user for the same window.

## With a stolen session and no password

- **Turn on 2FA for the victim.** Enroll and enable both succeeded. The victim's correct password then got "Invalid totp passcode", and a password reset by email did not help.
- **Mint long-lived credentials.** An API token and a CalDAV token created from the stolen session both still worked after the victim changed their password.
- **Outlive the password change.** After the change left zero sessions in the database, the stolen access token still read the user and tasks and minted another API token. It lasts up to 10 minutes by default; the middleware only checks signature and expiry (`pkg/routes/api_tokens.go:40`).

## What held

- The stolen refresh cookie was rejected after the password change.
- An API token granted every permission the server offers got 401 on all 14 endpoints, and could not mint tokens or enroll 2FA.

## Not covered

- Email change ran with the mailer off, so it applied immediately; the confirm-by-link path was not run here.
- The v1 export download returned 500 in the harness on a type assertion against the in-memory file store. I did not check whether that happens with real storage, so I am not counting it.

Full output is in `/tmp/claude-0/-exp-PREWORK-0c8u31w5-model-a/53e15d53-b32b-4f2b-bd51-f322f3934f44/scratchpad/sens1.log`.

content.text:
Two things get a blocked account back in: its bots, and the "email confirmation required" state, which blocks almost nothing except password login. I set up every credential type while the account was active, blocked it the way production does, and tried each again through the real router. Nothing is fixed, and the throwaway test is removed (tree clean).

## Results by credential

Disabled and locked behaved identically, so they share a column.

| Credential | Disabled or locked | Set to "unconfirmed" by an admin |
|---|---|---|
| Password login (v1, v2, by username or email) | Rejected | Rejected |
| Password on CalDAV | Rejected | Rejected |
| Refresh cookie (v1, v2) | Rejected | Rejected |
| OAuth refresh token | Rejected | Rejected |
| Existing session access token (default 10 min life) | Partly works, see below | Works for everything except change password |
| API token: REST v1/v2, CalDAV, Atom feeds, MCP | Rejected | **Works** |
| CalDAV token | Rejected | **Works** |
| OAuth access token | Rejected | **Works** |
| OAuth authorization code issued earlier | Rejected | **Works**, and yields a new session with a refresh token that keeps working |
| Link share the account created | Issues a token, but it cannot read the project | **Works** |
| API token of a bot the account owns | **Works**: read and created tasks in the owner's project | **Works** |
| Websocket auth with the old access token | Refused | Refused |

## The old access token while disabled or locked

- **Still allowed:**
  - listing labels, teams, notifications, own sessions, tokens and bots, and searching other users
  - creating a label
  - creating a link share on its own project, and sharing that project with another user
  - creating a bot
  - minting an API token, a CalDAV token, and an API token for a bot
- **Refused:** profile, projects, tasks, creating a project, team or comment, 2FA enroll, settings, password change, export, deletion.
- **The route back in:** a bot token minted this way worked immediately. A blocked user with a still-valid access token can give themselves lasting API access through a bot.

## Emailed links

- **Disabled:** asking for a reset email returns "This account is disabled", which tells anyone with the address its state. The reset link and the email-change link are both refused.
- **Locked:** the reset link unlocks the account, as designed. The email-change link is refused.
- **Fresh signup, never confirmed:** no credential but the password exists, and it is refused. A wrong password gets the same "Please confirm your email address" reply. The emailed reset link activates the account without the confirmation link.
- **Unconfirmed by admin:** the email-change link set the account back to active and switched it to the new address.

## After the block is lifted

Re-enabling by an admin, or unlocking by password reset, brought back:
- API and CalDAV tokens from before the block
- API tokens minted during it
- the pre-block access token
- an unredeemed OAuth code

Refresh cookies and OAuth refresh tokens stayed dead.

## Cause

- **Bots:** an API token is checked against the status of the bot that owns it, never the bot's human owner (`pkg/modules/auth/auth.go:276`), and blocking a user does not touch their bots.
- **Unconfirmed:** `finishLoadedUser` (`pkg/user/user.go:368`) rejects only disabled and locked. Password login is the one place that checks for unconfirmed (`pkg/user/user.go:421`), while the admin status change (`pkg/models/admin_user_actions.go:79`) assumes any non-active status blocks access.
- **Access token:** handlers that never load the user row accept it until it expires.

## How it was run

- **Disabled and unconfirmed:** set through the admin status endpoint.
- **Locked:** ten logins with the right password and a wrong 2FA code. The harness records events instead of delivering them, so I ran the session-revoking listener by hand.
- **Harness changes:** mailer on, per-IP rate floors raised so they would not mask results, and known-value email tokens planted because the real ones only exist in the email.
- **Not run:** OIDC and LDAP logins, which need an external server. The first websocket attempt failed because the harness had not started the hub; the table shows the rerun.

lastPrompt: Last area, the one-time secrets: 2fa codes and the links we email for confirmation, password reset and deletion. Can any of them be used more than once, or used after something else should have killed…

content.text:
The 2FA codes hold up, but the emailed links do not: several stay usable after events that should kill them, one race lets an account take an address nobody confirmed, and every link is written to the server log when opened. Nothing is fixed; the throwaway test, the Postgres container and its image are removed, and the tree is clean.

## Used more than once

| Secret | Used twice in a row | Used simultaneously |
|---|---|---|
| 2FA code | Rejected, including a code spent on enabling 2FA | 8 logins with one code: 1 succeeded |
| Password-reset link | Rejected, and using one link kills its siblings | 6 uses of one link: all 6 returned 200 |
| Signup confirmation link | Rejected | 6 uses: all 200 (same end state) |
| Email-change link | Rejected | Not run |
| Deletion link | Rejected | Not run |

- A 2FA code is accepted for the previous, current and next 30-second step.
- A token of one kind offered as another kind was rejected, as was a deletion link used from another user's session.

## Used after something should have killed it

- **Pending email change survives the owner securing the account.** This gave a full takeover:
  1. Someone with a session and the password requested a change to their own address.
  2. The owner got the notice and changed the password (I also ran it with a reset by email), leaving zero sessions.
  3. The intruder opened the emailed link, which needs no session, and the account moved to their address.
  4. They requested a reset to that address and logged in. The owner's new password no longer worked.
- **Reset link** still worked after each of these: a normal login, a password change in settings, an admin setting a new password, and the account moving to a new email address (the old mailbox's link still reset it).
- **Deletion link** still scheduled the deletion after the user pressed "cancel deletion" before confirming, and after a password change.
- **Expiry:**
  - Reset and deletion links 30 hours old still worked until the hourly cleanup job ran; the email says 24 hours, and nothing checks age at use.
  - The email-change link is checked at use; a 25-hour-old one was rejected.
  - A signup link 400 days old still worked, which the code comments say is intended.
- **Killed correctly:** the first email-change link after a second change, after a cancel, and after a resend.

## Email changes racing

- **Two changes at once:** safe. In 150 rounds one request always got the one-minute cooldown (429), and the pending address and live link always matched.
- **"Resend link" racing a change:** not safe. In 95 of 150 rounds both returned 200, leaving the pending address set to the second address while a live link sat in the first address's mailbox. In an earlier run I opened that link and the account took the second address, whose owner had confirmed nothing.
- **Cause:** the link is tied to the user, not to the address it was mailed to, so `ConfirmEmail` (`pkg/user/user_email_confirm.go:35`) applies whatever address is pending when it is used.

## Where the secrets end up

- **Database:** emailed tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes. The 2FA secret is stored in clear, twice (the `secret` and `url` columns of `totp`).
- **API:** the 2FA secret is returned at enrolment and by the status endpoint until 2FA is enabled, then hidden.
- **Mail:**
  - Reset and deletion links go to the current address.
  - The email-change link goes to the new address; the old one gets a notice without a link.
  - Each link is in both the text and HTML parts.
- **Server log:** opening a link is a GET with the token in the query string, and the request log (on by default) records the full URI. All three link types appeared there. Using a token via POST, the 2FA secret, and valid or wrong 2FA codes did not.
- **Notifications table:** none of the tokens.
- **Used-code markers:** kept in the key-value store, which is in-memory per process by default.

## How it was run

- **Requests and links:** real router, real mail rendering captured by the mail package's test hook, so the links are the ones a user receives.
- **Database:** Postgres 16 in a local container. On the default in-memory test database the real mail path locks up, and simultaneous requests are serialised.
- **Simulated time:** the one-minute cooldown and link ages were simulated by rewriting stored timestamps.
- **Read, not run:** what the frontend does with the link after load, and 2FA reuse across several server instances.

Full output is in `/tmp/claude-0/-exp-PREWORK-0c8u31w5-model-a/53e15d53-b32b-4f2b-bd51-f322f3934f44/scratchpad/secret2.log` and `/tmp/claude-0/-exp-PREWORK-0c8u31w5-model-a/53e15d53-b32b-4f2b-bd51-f322f3934f44/scratchpad/race.log`.
